# Repo guidance — Workshop (Git + VS Code) 📘

Summary
- This repository contains workshop content (lesson materials and recommendations), not a code product. Key files are `README.md`, `Github Workshop.md`, `Extensions for WD.md`, `Extensions for DS.md`, and a couple of graphic files (`Github Cycle Grafik.png` / `.canvas`).

When to edit these files
- Update `README.md` for high-level changes, links, or summary information.
- Update `Github Workshop.md` when changing Git command examples or the canonical Git/branching workflow used in the workshop.
- Update `Extensions for WD.md` or `Extensions for DS.md` when adding/removing recommended VS Code marketplace extensions. Follow the existing pattern (heading, short description, and a VS Marketplace link).
- Replace or add images (e.g., `Github Cycle Grafik.png`). If adding alternate formats, keep filenames consistent (same basename) so instructors can replace assets easily.

Branching and pull-request workflow (canonical)
- Branch naming: create a developer-scoped primary branch: `YOUR_NAME_Branch` (example: `veli_branch`).
- For a task, create a feature branch off your name branch: `YOUR_NAME_Branch/YOUR_TASK` (example: `veli_branch/update-extensions`).
- Common commands used in this repo (mirror `Github Workshop.md`):
  - Clone: `git clone <repo-url>` and `git pull`.
  - Setup name/email: `git config --global user.email "you@example.com" && git config --global user.name "Your Name"`
  - Create branches: `git switch -c YOUR_NAME_Branch` then `git switch -c YOUR_TASK/Feature_Title`.
  - Commit & push: `git add . && git commit -m "docs: <short message>" && git push`.
  - Update from main: `git pull origin main`.

Conventions for PRs and commits
- Use short commit prefixes: `docs:` for documentation changes, `chore:` for housekeeping. Keep messages concise (one-line summary).
- PR Summary should include: what changed, why (short context), and a list of files edited.
- Include a screenshot/preview for visual changes (e.g., graphics or markdown rendering).

Content Style & Patterns (What to follow exactly)
- Use a friendly, simple teaching tone for worksheets and instructions.
- Maintain the file structure and the simple markdown layout. Follow the existing syntax style used in `Extensions for WD.md` and `Extensions for DS.md` (H2 titles for items and direct VS Marketplace links).
- Preserve the hands-on examples from `Github Workshop.md` — the repository uses this as the canonical guide.
- Do not change educational instructions into technical, production quality documentation unless asked.

Validation & Preview
- Visual checks: Preview markdown changes in VS Code (Markdown Preview), verify link formats and the marketplace URLs.
- Linting: There is no automated linter or CI configured; a quick check is sufficient: run `markdownlint` if available locally, or run a link-checker for URLs.

When adding code or test files
- This repo currently contains no runnable code or CI. If adding code, include: a `README.md` section with run instructions, and add minimal test instructions. Avoid changing the root documentation style.

Examples (explicit)
- To add a new extension to `Extensions for WD.md`:
  1. Add an H2 heading with the extension name (e.g., `## NewExtension`).
  2. Include a 1-2 line description and a link to the VS Marketplace.
  3. Use similar phrasing and formatting as existing entries.

- To fix a typo in `Github Workshop.md`:
  1. Create a branch: `git switch -c veli_branch/typo-github-workshop`
  2. Correct the text (e.g. `begging` → `beginning`) and commit with message `docs: fix typo in Github Workshop.md`.
  3. Open a PR summarizing the change.

Limitations — what NOT to do
- Do not invent workflows or CI that do not exist. Because the repo has no CI or build workflows, any addition of these should be proposed as a separate task with migration steps and suggested configuration (e.g., add `.github/workflows/markdown-lint.yml`) rather than merged silently.
- Don’t remove or modify teacher instructions without preserving the educational meaning.

If you need more context from maintainers
- Keep PR descriptions short and tag the repository owner (`Valyo1907`) or the instructor.
- Prefer small, incremental PRs for clarity and easy review.

Contact & Followup
- If uncertain, suggest a change as a PR and add context in the body to prompt feedback from the instructor.

— End of instructions —
